chapter.name: Straight Lines
chapter.blurb: This chapter continues coordinate geometry by studying the straight line through algebra. It defines the inclination and slope of a line, gives the slope conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines and the angle between two lines, and develops the various forms of the equation of a line: horizontal and vertical lines, point-slope, two-point, slope-intercept and intercept forms, leading to the general equation Ax + By + C = 0. It closes with the distance of a point from a line and the distance between two parallel lines.

scope_in.item: Define the inclination of a line (angle with the positive x-axis, measured anticlockwise, 0 to 180 degrees) and the slope m = tan theta; state that a horizontal line has slope 0 and that the slope of a vertical line is not defined
Find the slope of the non-vertical line through two given points using m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1), and find a slope from a given inclination
Use the mid-point formula recalled from earlier classes as a tool inside slope and equation-of-line problems
Use m1 = m2 for parallel lines and m1 m2 = -1 for perpendicular non-vertical lines, including finding an unknown coordinate and classifying triangles and quadrilaterals by slopes
Decide whether three points are collinear by comparing slopes (slope of AB = slope of BC) or by checking that the third point satisfies the equation of the line through the other two
Find the acute angle between two lines from tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)| (1 + m1 m2 not 0), the obtuse angle as 180 degrees - theta, and an unknown slope from a given angle
Write the equations of horizontal and vertical lines, including the axes and lines through a given point parallel to an axis
Write the equation of a line in point-slope form y - y0 = m(x - x0) and in two-point form, and simplify it to ax + by + c = 0
Write the equation of a line in slope-intercept form y = mx + c, and in the form y = m(x - d) when the x-intercept d is given
Write the equation of a line in intercept form x/a + y/b = 1 and solve problems on intercepts (equal intercepts, given sum of intercepts, segment between the axes bisected at a point)
Recognise Ax + By + C = 0 (A and B not both zero) as the general equation of a line and rearrange it into slope-intercept or intercept form to read off the slope and the intercepts
Find the perpendicular distance of a point from a line using d = |Ax1 + By1 + C|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2), including finding points at a given distance from a line and the length of an altitude of a triangle
Find the distance between two parallel lines using |c1 - c2|/sqrt(1 + m^2) or |C1 - C2|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2), after making the coefficients of x and y the same

concepts.name: Inclination and slope of a line
concepts.description: Inclination of a line, slope m = tan theta, and the slope of the line through two given points.
concepts.idea: The inclination theta of a line is the angle it makes with the positive direction of the x-axis, measured anticlockwise (0 to 180 degrees). The slope is the tangent of that angle and measures the steepness and direction of the line.
concepts.rule: m = tan theta (theta not 90 degrees) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) for x1 not equal to x2. A horizontal line has slope 0; the slope of a vertical line is not defined.

concepts.name: Parallel and perpendicular lines; collinear points
concepts.description: Conditions for two non-vertical lines to be parallel or perpendicular in terms of slopes, and the slope test for three collinear points.
concepts.idea: Parallel lines have equal inclinations and therefore equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have inclinations differing by 90 degrees, which makes their slopes negative reciprocals.
concepts.rule: Non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if m1 = m2, and perpendicular if and only if m1 m2 = -1. Points A, B, C are collinear if and only if slope of AB = slope of BC.
concepts.example: The line through (-2, 6) and (4, 8) has slope 1/3, so any line perpendicular to it has slope -3.

For 4 and -4 the product is -16, not -1, so they are not perpendicular: the slope must be the negative reciprocal, not just the negative.

concepts.name: Angle between two lines
concepts.description: The acute and obtuse angles between two non-vertical lines found from their slopes.
concepts.idea: Two intersecting lines make two pairs of vertically opposite angles; adjacent angles add up to 180 degrees. The tangent of the angle between the lines comes from tan(alpha2 - alpha1).
concepts.rule: tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)| gives the acute angle theta, provided 1 + m1 m2 is not 0; the obtuse angle is 180 degrees - theta.
concepts.example: If the angle between two lines is 45 degrees and one slope is 1/2, then |(m - 1/2)/(1 + m/2)| = 1 gives m = 3 or m = -1/3.

questions.q: Explain why the formula for the acute angle between two lines, tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)|, contains an absolute value.
questions.a: The quantity (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) can be positive or negative. When it is positive it is the tangent of the acute angle between the lines; when it is negative it is the tangent of the obtuse angle, and the acute angle then has tangent equal to its negative. The tangent of an acute angle is always positive, so taking the absolute value gives tan of the acute angle in both cases.
s: States that (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) may be positive or negative, corresponding to the acute or the obtuse angle
States that tan of an acute angle is positive, so the absolute value gives the acute angle in both cases

questions.q: The slope of one line is double the slope of another line. If the tangent of the angle between them is 1/3, find the slopes of the lines.
questions.a: Let the slopes be m and 2m. Then |(2m - m)/(1 + 2m^2)| = 1/3, i.e. |m|/(1 + 2m^2) = 1/3, so 2m^2 - 3|m| + 1 = 0, which gives (2|m| - 1)(|m| - 1) = 0, so |m| = 1 or |m| = 1/2. Hence m = 1, -1, 1/2 or -1/2, and the pairs of slopes are 1 and 2, or -1 and -2, or 1/2 and 1, or -1/2 and -1.
s: Sets up |m/(1 + 2m^2)| = 1/3 with slopes m and 2m
Solves the positive case to get m = 1 or m = 1/2 (slopes 1, 2 or 1/2, 1)
Solves the negative case to get m = -1 or m = -1/2 (slopes -1, -2 or -1/2, -1)

questions.a: Both I and II

questions.q: Two lines pass through the point (2, 3) and intersect at an angle of 45 degrees. The slope of one line is 2. Find the possible slopes of the other line, and explain why there are two answers and how the two possible lines are related to each other.
questions.a: Let the other slope be m. Then |(m - 2)/(1 + 2m)| = tan 45 degrees = 1. Case 1: (m - 2)/(1 + 2m) = 1 gives m - 2 = 1 + 2m, so m = -3. Case 2: (m - 2)/(1 + 2m) = -1 gives m - 2 = -1 - 2m, so m = 1/3. There are two answers because a line can be turned through 45 degrees on either side of the given line, which is why the absolute value gives two cases. The two possible lines have slopes -3 and 1/3, whose product is -1, so they are perpendicular to each other.
s: Solves both cases: m = -3 and m = 1/3
Explains the two cases (either side of the given line) and notes (-3)(1/3) = -1, so the two lines are perpendicular

questions.q: For two lines Anu finds (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) = -sqrt(3) and concludes: 'The angle between the lines is 120 degrees, so there is no acute angle between them.' Evaluate her conclusion.
questions.a: Her conclusion is wrong. Two intersecting lines make two adjacent angles whose sum is 180 degrees. A value of -sqrt(3) means one of the angles is obtuse, 120 degrees; the other is 180 - 120 = 60 degrees, which is acute. Equivalently tan theta = |-sqrt(3)| = sqrt(3) gives the acute angle 60 degrees.
s: States that the lines make two adjacent angles adding to 180 degrees, so an obtuse angle of 120 degrees comes with an acute one

s: Rewrites the second line as 6x + 8y + 10 = 0 (same A and B)

questions.q: Find the equation of the line which is equidistant from the parallel lines 9x + 6y - 7 = 0 and 3x + 2y + 6 = 0.
questions.a: Write the second line with the same coefficients as the first: 9x + 6y + 18 = 0. A line equidistant from both is parallel to them, so let it be 9x + 6y + k = 0. Equal distances give |k - (-7)|/sqrt(117) = |k - 18|/sqrt(117), i.e. |k + 7| = |k - 18|. Since k + 7 = k - 18 is impossible, k + 7 = -(k - 18), so 2k = 11 and k = 11/2. The line is 9x + 6y + 11/2 = 0, i.e. 18x + 12y + 11 = 0.
s: Rewrites the second line as 9x + 6y + 18 = 0 and takes the required line as 9x + 6y + k = 0
Sets |k + 7| = |k - 18| using the distance between parallel lines and solves k = 11/2
Writes the line 18x + 12y + 11 = 0

questions.a: Only I

questions.q: Two opposite sides of a square lie along the lines 5x - 12y - 65 = 0 and 5x - 12y + 26 = 0. Find the area of the square, explaining why the distance between these lines gives the side of the square.
questions.a: Both lines have the same coefficients of x and y (A = 5, B = -12), so they are parallel. Opposite sides of a square are parallel and the perpendicular distance between them equals the side of the square. Distance = |C1 - C2|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2) = |-65 - 26|/sqrt(25 + 144) = 91/13 = 7 units. So the side is 7 units and the area is 7 x 7 = 49 square units.
s: Recognises the lines are parallel and that the distance between opposite sides equals the side of the square
Computes the distance |-65 - 26|/13 = 7
Finds the area 49 square units

questions.q: Tara finds the distance between the parallel lines 2x + y - 3 = 0 and 4x + 2y + 4 = 0 as |-3 - 4|/sqrt(2^2 + 1^2) = 7/sqrt(5). Evaluate her working.
questions.a: She is wrong. The formula |C1 - C2|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2) needs both equations to have the same coefficients of x and y. Dividing the second equation by 2 gives 2x + y + 2 = 0, so C2 = 2, not 4. The distance is |-3 - 2|/sqrt(4 + 1) = 5/sqrt(5) = sqrt(5) units.
s: Identifies the error: the two equations must first be written with the same A and B (second line is 2x + y + 2 = 0)
Gives the correct distance 5/sqrt(5) = sqrt(5)

questions.q: Construct the equations of two different lines parallel to the line 3x - 4y + 1 = 0, each at a distance of 2 units from it. Verify the distance for both lines.
questions.a: A line parallel to 3x - 4y + 1 = 0 has the form 3x - 4y + k = 0. Its distance from the given line is |k - 1|/sqrt(3^2 + (-4)^2) = |k - 1|/5. Setting |k - 1|/5 = 2 gives k - 1 = 10 or k - 1 = -10, so k = 11 or k = -9. The lines are 3x - 4y + 11 = 0 and 3x - 4y - 9 = 0. Check: |11 - 1|/5 = 2 and |-9 - 1|/5 = 2.
s: Writes a parallel line as 3x - 4y + k = 0 and sets |k - 1|/5 = 2
Solves both cases: k = 11 and k = -9
States both lines and verifies each distance is 2
